title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

errors: None decisive. The 'Cor. Main' is not proved on this page: Grothendieck himself asks whether it follows from the other axioms, and then promotes it to an axiom (At 11', then the more general At 12). So it is a postulate, not a corollary.

Notation drifts on this page: ≤ is used both for 'is a part of' (G ≤ F) and for the order on refinements (F'_G ≤ G', X'_K ≤ X'). Also ⊃ and ≤ are used interchangeably for figures. This makes the exact meaning of F' ∩ G' = F'_G ambiguous without the earlier definitions.
The phrase 'At 9' + At 10, on a' is an unfinished or misplaced fragment. It is probably meant as 'or At 9' + At 10'.

ideas.what: Reduction of gluing refinements over F∪G to the case of a sub-figure G⊂F, where compatibility is tested on restriction
ideas.modern_name: locality / amalgamation property for refinements (sheaf-type gluing of subdivisions)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in PL topology (common subdivisions of polyhedra agreeing on intersections); no single credit

ideas.what: Axiom At 11' / At 12: two refinements of compatible figures are compatible as soon as their restrictions to the intersection K = X∩Y are compatible
ideas.modern_name: local character of compatibility (overlap condition, cf. Mayer–Vietoris/amalgamation in a site of figures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: no direct counterpart; closest are o-minimal/tame-topology triangulation compatibility results (van den Dries, Shiota)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), without this axiomatics

ideas.what: Atelier axiomatics with the refinement posets X̃ constrained to a full subcategory Σ of ordered sets (Σ-atelier, next page)
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic 'tame' or 'stratified' geometry; abstract site of figures with refinement posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: unpublished Grothendieck; loosely comparable to o-minimal structures and Shiota's tame categories

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates an axiomatics ('ateliers', axioms At 9–12) for figures and their refinements, with a locality-of-compatibility axiom (At 12) designed to imply several earlier gluing and disjunction criteria. This axiomatic 'analysis situs' was never published or developed by others. On this page it is a step in sorting out which axioms are independent, and the question is left open.
missed.quote: Est-ce que ça résulte des autres axiomes ? ... At 12 Soient X' ≪ X et Y' ≪ Y dans M, avec X ≷ Y. Soit K = X ∩ Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a concrete fragment of Grothendieck's tame-topology foundations, beyond the Esquisse. It could be compared with o-minimal triangulation theory and with axiomatic PL/stratified frameworks. The independence question (does the main statement follow from At 9'/9''+At 10?) is an explicit open item.

deep.surprise_reason: The page belongs to an unpublished axiomatic framework (ateliers) for tame topology, which is of historical interest. The specific content, however, is axiom-juggling around a natural locality-of-compatibility condition that is standard in spirit (common subdivisions glue). The novelty lies in the framework, not in a striking result.
transcription_corrections: 'Cor. Main' (twice) is uncertain; since it is immediately followed by 'Est-ce que ça résulte des autres axiomes ?', it may read 'Conj.' or similar rather than a corollary.

The lines 'mais qui résulterait aussi de At 9'' + At 10. At 9' + At 10, on a' should probably read as one sentence: 'mais qui résulterait aussi de At 9' + At 10, ou de At 9'' + At 10' (line order in the image is interleaved).
'(Changeant le nom de At 11 en At 11')' is an insertion placed above the line 'C'est un renforcement considérable de At 10'.

The struck word at bottom left before 'avec X ≷ Y' is a deleted 'Supposons que'. The last line reads '(X'_K ≤ X', X'_K ≪ K et Y'_K ≤ Y', Y'_K ≪ K. Ceci', with the induced refinements written as subscripts K.
In the diagram, the subscript is X'_Y = X'|Y (with '||' meaning equality), and the second arrow from Y goes diagonally to Y'.
